claims.reason: src/config.ts checks legacy names before canonicalization in loadConfigForSetup and parseConfig, so a padded retired name is accepted and can be returned through providerConfig. Electron trims the same value in validateConnectorName/runtime detection, while browser-worker exact matching consumes the untrimmed provider identity; this is a reachable cross-layer connector identity split.

Exact legacy migration remains isolated to loadConfigForSetup and strict runtime parsing rejects exact retired identities. Existing guards close the exact-name case; they do not disprove the separate padded-name gap accepted from review1.

Mode/name consistency, distinct automatic/manual names, active tunnel presence, tunnel identity equality, and distinct tunnel IDs are enforced in src/config.ts and repeated by runtime-supervisor.cjs. No additional reachable invalid-state defect remains.

Automatic verification guards the connector before spawning, freshness is checked before positive readiness publication, manual mode reports selection as a warning, and helper cleanup preserves the primary error with cleanup detail. The claimed false-readiness and hidden-primary-error paths are closed.

roots.title: Connector names are compared before config canonicalization
roots.trigger: Persist a connector identity with leading or trailing whitespace, especially a retired name such as "Codex Native3 ".
roots.fix: Canonicalize connector fields at the config boundary before migration, legacy detection, equality checks, and provider projection, or reject non-canonical whitespace. Preserve the public connector names and ABI.
